spans.s:
शिंशपा शिंशपा or (according to some)
शिंशिपा, f. the tree Dalbergia Sisu; the Aśoka tree.
सिंसपा सिंसपा, f. = शिंशपा, q. v.

शिंशुमार शिंशुमार, अस्, m., Ved. a por-
poise (= शिशु-मार).
शिंह् शिंह् = rt. शिङ्घ्, q. v.
शिंहाण, शिंहाणक, = शिङ्घाण, &c.
शिनि शिनि, इस्, m. (according to Uṇādi-s.
IV. 51

. fr. rt. 1. शी), N. of a son of Sumitra; of a
descendant of Garga (a chief of the Kṣatriya tribe);
a man belonging to a particular class of Kṣatriyas;
(अयस्), m. pl., N. of a class of Kṣatriyas; [cf.
शैन्य.]
—शिनि-बाहु, N. of a river.
—शिनेर्-
नप्तृ, ता, m. ‘grandson of Śini,’ N. of Sātyaki
(one of the Pāṇḍu chiefs).

शीन शीन, अस्, आ, अम् (fr. rt. श्यै, cf. शीत),
congealed, thick (as oil or butter); (अस्), m. a fool,
blockhead; a large snake.
शीन, अस्, आ, अम्. See p. 1010, col. 3.
सिन सिन, अस्, m. (according to Uṇādi-s.
III. 2
. fr. rt. सि, ‘to bind;’ see also Nirukta

),
‘a quantity of anything bound or collected together,’
a lump of food, &c., mouthful; (अम्), n. the body;
food (Ved.; Sāy. = अन्न); (अस्, ई, अम्), white,
white-coloured (according to Śabda-k.); blind with
one eye, one-eyed, = काण; (ई), f. white, (perhaps
an old fem. of 2. सित; cf. श्येनी under श्येन.)
—सिन-वत्, आन्, अती, अत्, Ved. having food.
सिंह सिंह, अस्, m. (in Uṇādi-s.

. said
to be fr. rt. 1. सिच्, with ह substituted for the final and
a nasal inserted; according to others fr. सिह्, a weakened
form of rt. 1. सह्, with insertion of nasal), a lion; the
sign of the zodiac Leo or the Lagna of that sign (see
लग्न); a hero or any eminent person, (often used
at the end of comps. to express excellence or emi-
nence of any kind, cf. पुरुष-स्˚, राज-स्˚); the
symbol or emblem of the twenty-fourth Arhat of
the present Ava-sarpiṇī; a particular plant (= रक्त-
शिग्रु); N. of a king (father of Sāhideva); (आ), f. a
particular grass or plant, = नाडी; (ई), f. a lioness, &c.,
see p. 1113, col. 1.
—सिंह-कारक, अस्, m. a creator
of lions.
—सिंह-केलि, इस्, m., N. of a celebrated
Bodhi-sattva (= Mañju-ghoṣa).
—सिंह-केशर or
सिंह-केसर, अस्, m. a lion's mane; the plant
Mimusops Elengi; a kind of Modaka or sweetmeat.
—सिंह-ग, अस्, m. ‘lion-going,’ epithet of Śiva.
—सिंह-गुप्त, अस्, m. = सङ्घ-गुप्त, q. v.
—सिंह-ग्रीव, अस्, आ, अम्, lion-necked.
—सिंह-
घोष, अस्, m. a proper N.
—सिंह-तल, अस्, m.
(probably for संह-तल, q. v.), the open hands
joined.
—सिंह-तुण्ड, अस्, m. ‘lion-faced,’ a kind
of fish; a particular plant (= सेहुण्ड).
—सिंह-
दंष्ट्र, अस्, आ, अम्, lion-tusked, having the teeth
of a lion; (अस्), m. epithet of Śiva.
—सिंह-दत्त,
अस्, m. ‘lion-given,’ N. of a poet.
—सिंह-दर्प,
अस्, आ, अम्, having a lion's pride, proud as a lion.
—सिंह-द्वार, अम्, n. a principal gate, chief gate,
any gate or entrance.
—सिंह-ध्वनि, इस्, m. the
roar of a lion; a sound like the roar of a lion; a
war-cry.
—सिंह-नर्दिन्, ई, इनी, इ, roaring like a
lion.
—सिंह-नाद, अस्, m. a lion's roar; a war-cry,
war-whoop; a species of the Ati-jagatī metre (=
कल-हंस); ‘roaring like a lion,’ epithet of Śiva.
—सिंह-नादक, अस्, m. the roar of a lion; a war-
cry; (इका), f. a particular prickly plant (= दुर्-
आलभा).
—सिंह-पर्णी, f. ‘lion-leaved,’ the plant
Justicia Ganderussa (= वासक).
—सिंह-पिप्पली,
f. a kind of plant (= सैंहली).
—सिंह-पुच्छिका,
f. ‘lion-tailed,’ a particular plant (= चित्र-पर्णिका).
—सिंह-पुच्छी, f. the plant Citra-parṇikā; other
plants (= पृश्नि-पर्णी; = माष-पर्णी).
—सिंह-
पुष्पी, f. a kind of plant (= पृश्नि-पर्णी).
—सिंह-प्रगर्जन, अस्, आ, अम्, roaring like a
lion.
—सिंह-प्रगर्जित, अम्, n. the roaring or
roar of a lion.
—सिंह-प्रदीप, अस्, m., N. of a
work mentioned in the Kuṇḍa-kaumudī.
—सिंह-
बाहु, उस्, m., N. of the father of Vijaya (the founder
of the first Buddhist dynasty in Ceylon).
—सिंह-
मुखी, f. a kind of plant (= वासक).
—सिंह-
याना, f. or सिंह-रथा, f. ‘having a lion as a
vehicle,’ N. of the goddess Durgā.
—सिंह-रव,
अस्, m. the cry or roar of a lion.
—सिंहर्षभ
(˚ह-ऋष्˚), अस्, m. a noble or fierce lion.
—सिंह-
लग्न, अम्, n. the Lagna of the sign Leo, (see
लग्न.)
—सिंह-लम्ब, N. of a place.
—सिंह-
लील, अस्, m. a particular kind of sexual union.
—सिंह-वाहन, अस्, m. ‘having a lion for a
vehicle,’ epithet of Śiva.
—सिंह-वाहिनी, f. ‘borne
on a lion,’ epithet of Durgā.
—सिंह-विक्रम, अस्,
m. = विक्रम-सिंह.
—सिंह-विक्रान्त, अस्, आ,
अम्, valiant as a lion; (अस्), m. a horse.
—सिंह-
विक्रान्त-गति, इस्, इस्, इ, or सिंह-विक्रान्त-गामिन्,
ई, इनी, इ, having a gait as bold as a lion's.
—सिंह-
विक्रीडित, अम्, n. ‘lion's play,’ a kind of metre.
—सिंह-विन्ना, f. a kind of plant (= माष-पर्णी).
—सिंह-व्याघ्र-निषेवित, अस्, आ, अम्, inhabited
by lions and tigers.
—सिंह-शाव, अस्, or सिंह-शिशु,
[]
उस्, m. a lion's whelp or cub.
—सिंह-संहनन,
अम्, n. the killing or destroying of a lion; (अस्, आ,
अम्), lion-shaped, well-shaped, handsome; strong as a
lion.
—सिंह-स्कन्ध, अस्, आ, अम्, ‘lion-shouldered,’
having the shoulders of a lion.
—सिंह-स्थ, अस्, m.
‘being in the lion,’ epithet of the planet Jupiter
when in the constellation Leo.
—सिंहाढ्य (˚ह-
आढ्˚), अस्, आ, अम्, abounding in lions.
—सिंहाव-
लोकन (˚ह-अव्˚), अम्, n. a lion's look (applied to
the habit of constantly pausing and looking back).
—सिंहासन (˚ह-आस्˚), अम्, n. ‘lion-seat,’ a throne
(said to be so called as supported by golden lions);
(अस्), m. a particular kind of sexual union.
—सिंहा-
सन-चक्र, अम्, n., N. of three astrological dia-
grams shaped like a man and marked with the
twenty-seven Nakṣatras.
—सिंहासन-द्वात्रिंशत्,
त्, or सिंहासनद्वात्रिंशत्-पुत्त्रिका-वार्त्ता, f., N.
of a work consisting of thirty-two stories in praise of
Vikramāditya (= विक्रम-चरित).
—सिंहासन-
भ्रष्ट, अस्, आ, अम्, fallen from a throne, dethroned.
—सिंहासन-रण, अस्, अम्, m. n. a strife or struggle
for the throne.
—सिंहासन-स्थ, अस्, आ, अम्, sitting
on a throne.
—सिंहास्य (˚ह-आस्˚), अस्, आ, अम्, lion-
faced; (अस्), m. a kind of plant (= वासक); a par-
ticular position of the hands.
—सिंहोद्धता (˚ह-
उद्˚), f. a kind of metre.
—सिंहोन्नता (˚ह-उन्˚),
f. a kind of metre.

सिंहल, अम्, n. tin; brass; bark, rind; Cassia
bark; (अम्, आ), n. f. the island or country of Ceylon,
(perhaps so called as abounding in lions); (आस्), m.
pl. the people of Ceylon.
—सिंहल-द्वीप, अस्, m. the
island of Ceylon.
—सिंहल-स्थ, अस्, आ, अम्, being
or dwelling in Ceylon; (आ), f. a kind of plant (=
सर्प-दण्डा, सैंहली).
—सिंहला-स्थान, अस्,
m. a kind of plam tree.
सिंहलक, अम्, n. the island of Ceylon.

सिंहाय, Nom. A. सिंहायते, -यितुम्, to be or
become like a lion, act like a lion.

सिंहिका, f., N. of the mother of Rāhu, (she was
one of the thirteen daughters of Dakṣa and wife of
Kaśyapa); N. of a daughter of Kaśyapa (wife of
Vipracitti).
—सिंहिका-सूनु, उस्, m. ‘son of Siṃ-
hikā,’ epithet of Rāhu or the Ascending Node per-
sonified.

सिंहिकेय, अस्, m. ‘son of Siṃhikā,’ epithet of
Rāhu.

सिंही, f. a lioness; N. of the mother of Rāhu;
of various plants (= वार्ताकी; = कण्टकारी; = वा-
सक; = बृहती; = मुद्ग-पर्णी).
—सिंही-लता,
f. a kind of plant (= बृहती).

सिंहाणक, अस्, अम्, m. n. = सिंहाण above, (also
written सिङ्घाणक, शिङ्घाणक, सङ्घाणक.)
सिंहान, अम्, n. = सिंहाण above.

सिनीवाली, f. (said to be connected with सिनी,
‘white;’ but in Nirukta
XI. 31

. सिनी is connected
with rt. सि and वाली with rt. वल्, ‘to surround,’ or
with बाल, ‘young;’ the real meaning may be ‘a
white ring’), the day preceding that of new moon
or the day on which the moon rises with a thin
crescent of light scarcely visible; N. of a Vedic god-
dess; of the goddess Durgā.

सिन्दुक सिन्दुक, अस्, m. (probably fr. rt.
स्यन्द्, see below), the small tree or shrub Vitex
Negundo.

सिन्दु-वार, अस्, m. (probably for स्यन्द-वार,
the plant being used medicinally to prevent flow
of the humors and laxity), = सिन्दुक above; [cf.
सिन्धु-वार.]
सिन्दूर सिन्दूर, अस्, m. (in Uṇādi-s.

.
said to be fr. rt. स्यन्द्), a sort of tree; (ई), f., N.
of a plant (= रोचनी); the plant Grislea Tomentosa
(= धातकी); the plant Lythrum Fruticosum; red
cloth or clothes; (अम्), n. red lead, minium, ver-
milion; = राज-लेख (according to some).
—सिन्-
दूर-कारण, अम्, n. ‘origin of minium,’ lead.
—सिन्दूर-तिलक, अस्, m. ‘marked with red lead,’
an elephant; (आ), f. a woman whose forehead is
marked with red lead (and therefore whose husband
is living).
—सिन्दूर-निर्गम, अस्, m., N. of the
137th chapter of the Krīḍā-khaṇḍa or second part
of the Gaṇeśa-Purāṇa.
—सिन्दूर-पुष्पी, f. a kind
of plant (= वीर-पुष्पी).
सिन्दूरिका, f. red lead, minium.
सिन्दूरित, अस्, आ, अम्, reddened, made red.

सिन्धु सिन्धु, उस्, m. (probably connected
with rt. स्यन्द्, ‘to flow’), the ocean, sea, (कृपा-
सिन्धु, ‘ocean of mercy,’ a term for an exceedingly
merciful person); N. of Varuṇa (as god of the
ocean); the river Indus; the Indus personified (as
one of the male rivers, cf. नद); the country
around the Indus (commonly called Sindh); the water
into which the Soma drops; water ejected from the
mouth or from an elephant's trunk (= वमथु);
the juice that exudes from an elephant's temples; an
elephant; a particular Rāga or musical mode (re-
garded as son of the Rāga Mālakauśa); the tree
Vitex Negundo [cf. सिन्दुक]; white or refined
borax, = श्वेत-टङ्कण; (अवस्), m. pl. the in-
habitants of Sindh; (उस्), f. the river Sindhu, (Ni-
rukta
IX. 26

); a river or stream of water in general.
—सिन्धु-कफ, अस्, m. ‘sea-foam,’ cuttle-fish
bone.
—सिन्धु-कर, अम्, n. a kind of white borax
(= श्वेत-टङ्कण).
—सिन्धु-क्षित्, त्, m., N. of
the author of the hymn Ṛg-veda

(having the
patronymic Praiyamedha).
—सिन्धु-खेल, अस्, m.
‘sported or flowed over by the Indus,’ the country
Sindh.
—सिन्धु-ज, अस्, आ, अम्, ocean-born, sea-
born, marine; river-born, aquatic; born or produced
in the country Sindh; (आ), f. epithet of the goddess
Lakṣmī (as produced at the churning of the ocean);
(अम्), n. rock-salt.
—सिन्धु-जन्मन्, आ, आ, अ,
ocean-born, sea-born; produced in Sindh; (आ), m.
[]
the moon; (अ), n. rock-salt.
—सिन्धु-डा, f., N.
of the wife of the Rāga Mālava.
—सिन्धु-देश, अस्,
m. the country of Sindh.
—सिन्धु-द्वीप, अस्, m.,
N. of a king; of the author of the hymn Ṛg-veda

(having the patronymic Āmbarīṣa).
—सिन्धु-
नद, N. of a river.
—सिन्धु-नन्दन, अस्, m. ‘son
of the ocean,’ the moon (fabled to have been one
of the fourteen precious things recovered at the churn-
ing of the ocean, see मन्दर, p. 746).
—सिन्धु-
नाथ, अस्, m. ‘lord of rivers,’ the ocean.
—सिन्धु-
पति, इस्, m. ‘lord of Sindh,’ epithet of Jayad-ratha.
—सिन्धु-पार-ज, अस्, आ, अम्, born or produced
on the further bank of the Indus.
—सिन्धु-पुत्र,
अस्, m. ‘son of the ocean,’ the moon; a sort of
ebony.
—सिन्धु-पुलिन्द, आस्, m. pl., N. of a
people.
—सिन्धु-पुष्प, अस्, m. ‘sea-flower,’ a
conch-shell.
—सिन्धु-मध्य, N. of a district.
—सिन्धु-मन्थ, अस्, m. the churning of the
ocean, (see मन्दर, p. 746); ‘ocean churning-
stick,’ a mountain (according to some).
—सिन्धु-
मन्थ-ज, अम्, n. rock-salt.
—सिन्धु-मातृ, ता,
त्री, तृ, Ved. having the sea as mother (said of the
Soma, also of the Maruts and of the Aśvins); (ता), f.
‘mother of streams,’ epithet of the river Sarasvatī
(Ved.).
—सिन्धु-मुख, अम्, n. the mouth of a
river.
—सिन्धु-मुखागत (˚ख-आग्˚), अस्, आ,
अम्, arrived at the mouth of a river.
—सिन्धु-
राज, अस्, m. ‘king of Sindh,’ epithet of Jayad-
ratha.
—सिन्धु-लवण, अम्, n. ‘Sindh-salt,’ rock-
salt.
—सिन्धु-वार, अस्, m. a good horse or one
of a particularly good breed (brought probably from
Sindh or the borders of Persia); the small tree Vitex
Negundo (= सिन्दु-वार).
—सिन्धु-वारक, अस्,
m. Vitex Negundo, (see above.)
—सिन्धु-वारित,
अस्, m. Vitex Negundo, (see above.)
—सिन्धु-वासिन्,
ई, इनी, इ, living in Sindh, an inhabitant of Sindh.
—सिन्धु-वाहस्, आस्, आस्, अस्, Ved. bringing streams
of water.
—सिन्धु-वेषण, अस्, m. the tree Gme-
lina Arborea.
—सिन्धु-शयन, अस्, m. ‘ocean-
reclining,’ epithet of Viṣṇu.
—सिन्धु-सङ्गम,
अस्, m. ‘sea-confluence,’ the mouth of a river or its
point of junction with the sea.
—सिन्धु-समुद्र-
सङ्गम, अस्, m., N. of a place.
—सिन्धु-सूनु,
उस्, m. ‘son of Sindhu,’ N. of the Asura Jalan-dhara.
—सिन्धु-सौवीर, आस्, m. pl., N. of a people (the
people of Sindh and western Rājputāna, according
to some).
—सिन्धूत्थ (˚धु-उत्˚) or सिन्धूद्-
भव (˚धु-उद्˚), अम्, n. ‘Sindh-produced,’ rock-
salt (= सैन्धव).
—सिन्धूपल (˚धु-उप्˚),
अम्, n. ‘Sindh-stone,’ rock-salt.

सिन्धुक, अस्, आ, अम्, marine; born or produced
in Sindh; (अस्), m. the tree Vitex Negundo [cf. सिन्-
दुक]; N. of a king (= शूद्रक).

सिन्धुर, अस्, m. an elephant; [cf. सिन्धु.]
—सिन्धुर-द्वेषिन्, ई, m. ‘elephant-hater,’ a lion.
सिन्धुल, अस्, m., N. of the father of Bhoja.
सिन्व् सिन्व् = rt. निन्व्, q. v.
